latin: Peccatum Soddomae_fuit per truncationem ultimae plantae.
latin_note: Farmer's transcription shows an underscore, 'Soddomae_fuit'; read as two words, 'Soddomae fuit' (farmer1998:18198). Wirszubski's quotation of the same conclusio reads 'Peccatum Soddomae fuit per truncationem ultimae plantae' without the underscore (wirszubski1989:2690).
translation: The sin of Sodom occurred through the truncation of the last plant.
translation_note: 'truncationem ultimae plantae' is left literal, 'the truncation of the last plant' (farmer1998:18198); the packet consulted does not gloss which sefirah 'the last plant' names, so no symbolic equivalence is supplied here.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch12, from Latin at farmer1998:18198

sources.pico_relation: Wirszubski cross-refers the thesis to Recanati fol. 51ra-b on this passage

doctrine: Farmer's note ties the thesis to Genesis 18:20 and following, the narrative of Sodom's condemnation, and directs the reader to thesis 28.4 for 'the symbolism of the "severing of the shoots"' (paraphrase, farmer1998:18273). Thesis 28.4 itself states, in Pico's Latin, that 'the sin of Adam was a truncation of the kingdom from the other plants' (farmer1998:17544), so Farmer's cross-reference sets Sodom's sin and Adam's sin as parallel instances of a 'truncation' involving 'plants' in Pico's Kabbalistic vocabulary, without his note here specifying what the plants or the truncation represent (farmer1998:18273).
historiography: Wirszubski quotes the thesis as his 'Conclusio XXXVI' and cross-refers it to Recanati, fol. 51ra-b, as the passage interpreting Genesis 18:20-21 (wirszubski1989:2690).

quotations.text: Peccatum Soddomae fuit per truncationem ultimae plantae.

not_established: What 'the last plant' (ultima planta) symbolizes in Pico's sefirotic vocabulary is not stated in the material consulted; not established by the sources consulted.
The content of Recanati's fol. 51ra-b, beyond Wirszubski's cross-reference to it, is not established by the sources consulted.
